Acme Postpones Lumen Hub Launch Again

By Alex Example · 22 October 2026

Acme appears to be postponing the launch of its Lumen Hub once again. Instead of next month, the crowdfunding campaign is now expected to start in the first quarter of next year, according to an updated notice on the product page.

The Lumen Hub is meant to combine a local smart home hub with support for several wireless standards and a voice assistant that runs on the device. Acme first announced it in the summer, with a planned launch in September, which it then moved to November.

Why the delay?

The company did not give a detailed reason. A spokesperson said the team wants to "finish certification and polish the voice assistant before backers receive their units". Certification for the new protocol version typically takes several weeks.

Early-bird prices are said to remain unchanged. Interested buyers can still register on the product page to receive a discount code when the campaign goes live.

We would rather ship a few weeks later than ship something half finished.

Whether the second postponement will be the last remains to be seen. We will update this article once Acme confirms a firm date.
